# 1 Maccabees Chapter 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 7

---

## Council Notes

**On the Hasideans (v.13):** The Hasideans make their second appearance, here being the first to seek peace and being the victims of Alcimus's treachery. Their theological reasoning is revealing: since a legitimate Aaronide priest has come, they assume political safety. The author records their catastrophic misjudgment without editorial comment — the massacre speaks.

**On the psalm-citation (vv.16-17):** The quotation (*"the flesh of your holy ones..."*) is from Psalm 79:2-3. The author explicitly introduces it as scripture (*kata ton logon hon egrapse*). This is a remarkable moment: the author interprets current events through scriptural categories, placing Alcimus's massacre in the same category as the Babylonian destruction.

**On Nicanor's threat (v.35):** The threat to burn the temple if Judas is not delivered is the narrative pivot of the second half of the chapter. It sets up Nicanor as the culminating villain who compounds military opposition with direct sacrilege.

**On "Nicanor's Day" (vv.43-49):** The author records the establishment of "Nicanor's Day" (13 Adar) as a permanent festival. This festival is otherwise attested in 2 Maccabees 15 and in Megillat Ta'anit. The date is the day before Purim, which created later complications for the Jewish calendar. The chapter ends with characteristic understatement: "the land had rest for a little while."

**On the 185,000 (v.41):** The prayer references the angel that struck down the Assyrian army in 2 Kings 19:35 (Isaiah 37:36). This is the standard "Holy War" prayer — Judas asks God to repeat past miracles. The number is preserved exactly.

---

1. In the one hundred and fifty-first year, Demetrius son of Seleucus escaped from Rome, arrived with a few men at a coastal city, and seized the throne.
2. As he was entering the royal palace of his ancestors, the troops seized Antiochus and Lysias to hand them over to him.
3. When this was reported to him, he said: "Do not let me see their faces."
4. So the troops killed them, and Demetrius took his seat on the throne.
5. Then all the lawless and ungodly men of Israel came to him, led by Alcimus, who wanted to be high priest.
6. They laid charges against the people before the king, saying: "Judas and his brothers have destroyed all your friends and driven us out of our own land.
7. Now send someone you trust to go and see all the destruction Judas has brought upon us and upon the king's territory, and to punish him and all who support him."
8. The king chose Bacchides, one of the king's Friends who governed the Great Plain — a powerful man, faithful to the king — and sent him.
9. He also sent with him the ungodly Alcimus, confirmed to him the high priesthood, and ordered him to exact vengeance on the Israelites.
10. They set out and advanced with a large force into the land of Judah. Bacchides sent messengers to Judas and his brothers with peaceable words — spoken in deceit.
11. But they paid no attention, for they saw that he had come with a large force.
12. Then a company of scribes came together to Alcimus and Bacchides to seek a just settlement.
13. The Hasideans were the first among the Israelites to seek peace with them; for they said: "A priest of the lineage of Aaron has come with the army, and he will not do us wrong."
14. Alcimus spoke peaceful words to them and swore an oath: "We will not seek to harm you or your friends."
15. They trusted him. But he seized sixty of them and killed them in a single day, in accordance with the word that was written:
16. "The flesh of your faithful ones and their blood they poured out all around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them."
17. Terror and dread fell upon all the people; for they said: "There is no truth or justice in them — they have broken the agreement and the oath they swore."
18. Bacchides withdrew from Jerusalem and camped at Beth-zaith. He had many of those who had deserted him seized, killed some of the people, and threw them into the great cistern.
19. He put the country in Alcimus's charge, left troops to support him, and returned to the king.
20. Alcimus fought to hold his grip on the high priesthood.
21. All who were disrupting their people gathered to him; they gained control of the land of Judah and inflicted great harm on Israel.
22. Judas saw all the harm that Alcimus and those with him had done to the Israelites — harm worse than the Gentiles had done.
23. He went out into all the surrounding territory of Judea, taking vengeance on the deserters; and they were cut off from going through the land.
24. When Alcimus saw that Judas and his men were gaining strength, and that he could not hold out against them, he returned to the king and brought many charges against them.
25. The king sent Nicanor, one of his honored princes — a man hostile to Israel and bitter against them — with orders to destroy the people.
26. Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a large force and sent deceitfully peaceable words to Judas and his brothers:
27. "Let there be no battle between us. I will come with a few men so that we may meet face to face in peace."
28. He came to Judas, and they greeted one another peaceably; but the enemy was ready to seize Judas.
29. When Judas learned that Nicanor had come to him with treachery, he was afraid and refused to meet him again.
30. When Nicanor realized his plan had been discovered, he advanced to meet Judas in battle near Capharsalama.
31. About five hundred of Nicanor's men fell, and the survivors fled to the city of David.
32. After these events Nicanor went up to Mount Zion. Some of the priests from the sanctuary and some of the elders of the people came out to greet him in peace,
33. and to show him the burnt offering being offered on behalf of the king.
34. But he mocked them, derided them, defiled them, and spoke arrogantly.
35. In great wrath he swore an oath: "Unless Judas and his army are delivered into my hands, when I return in safety I will burn down this house." He went out in a violent rage.
36. The priests went in, stood before the altar and the temple, and wept, saying:
37. "You chose this house to bear your name, to be a house of prayer and supplication for your people.
38. Take vengeance on this man and his army; let them fall by the sword. Remember their blasphemies, and do not let them endure."
39. Nicanor left Jerusalem and camped at Beth-horon; and the Syrian army came to reinforce him there.
40. Judas camped at Adasa with three thousand men. He prayed and said:
41. "When the messengers of the king blasphemed, your angel went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand of them.
42. Crush this army before us in the same way today; let the rest know that he has spoken wickedly against your sanctuary; and judge him according to his wickedness."
43. On the thirteenth day of the month of Adar the two armies met in battle; Nicanor's army was defeated, and Nicanor himself was the first to fall.
44. When his army saw that Nicanor had fallen, they threw down their weapons and fled.
45. The Judean forces pursued them a full day's journey from Adasa to Gazara, sounding the signal trumpets behind them.
46. Men came out from all the surrounding villages of Judea; they outflanked the enemy and turned them back on themselves; they all fell by the sword, and not one of them was left.
47. Then the Judeans collected the plunder and the spoils; they cut off Nicanor's head and his right arm, which he had stretched out with arrogance, and brought them and hung them up near Jerusalem.
48. The people rejoiced greatly and kept that day as a day of great gladness.
49. They ordained that this day should be observed every year on the thirteenth of Adar.
50. And the land of Judah had rest for a little while.
